items.abstract: <jats:p>Natural-language commands allow Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies to connect human intent with embodied control, but a policy can lose the intended visual referent while generating an action sequence. Such failures are hard to inspect because transformers expose many attention tensors whose shapes and roles differ across the vision-language backbone and action expert. We introduce fused attention graph (FAG)-VLA, an inference-time method that places heterogeneous cross-modal attention ffows in a relation-speciffc comparison space and represents the selected native ffows as a directed graph. A lightweight MLP converts attention blocksfrom multiple layers and headsinto ffxedlength codes. FAG-VLA compares these codes separately for each directed modality pair, retrieves the most informative native block, and derives interpretable graph-edge weights without substituting projected values for the original attention mass. The graph sequence produced over ffow-matching steps yields a language-vision coherence index (LVCI) that tracks whether grounding remains stable as actions are formed. An LVCI trend trigger, protected by ffoor, cooldown, and revert rules, invokes an LLM to clarify the instruction when the observed grounding deteriorates. On LIBERO, FAGVLA attains a 95.8% task success rate, exceeding the evaluated state-of-the-art baselines. The method therefore supplies an observable feedback signal for closed-loop correction while leaving the VLA parameters unchanged. The code is available at https://github.com/fagvlaofffcial/fag_vla</jats:p>
title: FAG-VLA: Vision-Language-Action Model With Fused Attention Graph for Robustly Following Natural-Language Instructions

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
      
        We propose a neural sequence-to-sequence model for direction following, a task that is essential to realizing effective autonomous agents. Our alignment-based encoder-decoder model with long short-term memory recurrent neural networks (LSTM-RNN) translates natural language instructions to action sequences based upon a representation of the observable world state. We introduce a multi-level aligner that empowers our model to focus on sentence "regions" salient to the current world state by using multiple abstractions of the input sentence. In contrast to existing methods, our model uses no specialized linguistic resources (e.g., parsers) or task-specific annotations (e.g., seed lexicons). It is therefore generalizable, yet still achieves the best results reported to-date on a benchmark single-sentence dataset and competitive results for the limited-training multi-sentence setting. We analyze our model through a series of ablations that elucidate the contributions of the primary components of our model.
      
    </jats:p>
title: Listen, Attend, and Walk: Neural Mapping of Navigational Instructions to Action Sequences
